A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SafeConstellations and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. All 13 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2 support reliable matching despite title, terminology, and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original task-over-refusal evaluations, LLaMA and Qwen steering experiments, component ablations, MMLU results, and representation analyses in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds latency measurements and quantitative representation-separation analyses in Appendices A.2.1 and A.3.2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces target-centroid cosine similarity averaged across all layers with target-minus-refusal cosine similarity averaged across retained task layers. Equation 4 reverses the target/refusal distance ratio, changing layer selection, and Algorithm 2 removes the global fallback pattern. These revise central procedural decisions; the PDFs do not establish whether the experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both retain the 1,047-sample benchmark covering the same nine text types and five tasks, sourced from Alpaca, XSTest, JailbreakBench, SaladBench, and custom RAG-QA data, plus MMLU. The new representation and timing analyses introduce no distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen1.5-7B baselines and component-removal, fixed-layer, late-layer, and final-layer comparisons. Newly cited mitigation methods are discussed without being added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 introduces protocols for layer-wise silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, and centroid-distance measurements, individual-sample trajectory analysis, and latency comparisons against response length. The original stratified 75/25 split, stated 270-example test evaluation, model configurations, and refusal/MMLU metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3.2 substantially extends the mechanistic analysis beyond centroid visualizations through individual trajectories and quantitative comparisons of task-specific versus pooled separation (Figures 12–14 and Table 5). Appendix A.2.1 adds computational-overhead analysis. Existing component ablations and qualitative failure examples are retained, including the relocated qualitative table.

E5.justification: The new latency boxplots in Figure 5 add descriptive variability reporting through medians, quartiles, whiskers, and outliers. Both versions retain seed 42; v2 introduces no repeated-run confidence intervals or significance tests. The boxplots describe sample variability rather than demonstrated run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: V2 adds quantitative geometry and computational-cost results: Table 5 reports L16 silhouette scores of 0.158 for sentiment, 0.143 for translation, and 0.094 pooled; Figure 5 reports latency distributions, and the text adds memory and small-sample adaptation findings. Existing efficacy results remain identical, including Table 2's LLaMA over-refusal rate of 4.81% and MMLU accuracy of 46.57%. These are added result families, not demonstrated efficacy gains.

T1.justification: The task-score definition in Algorithm 1 and steering-potential definition in Equation 4 change mathematically. Other central definitions remain equivalent, including the unchanged formula renamed from Trajectory Health to Layer Alignment. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and v2 adds no substantial theoretical development.

C1.justification: V2 narrows the introduction's claim that constellations are invariant to input content and reflect only task intent to stability across input variations and primarily reflecting the task. The conclusion drops the explicit suggestion of applications beyond over-refusal mitigation. The benchmark, selective steering contribution, and up-to-73% reduction claim remain.

C2.justification: New Section 6.1 provides substantive limitations concerning internal-model access, static and model-specific embeddings, limited attack coverage, MMLU's incomplete utility assessment, heuristic choices, and judge bias. The appendix additionally discusses unsupported batching, open-ended-task generalization, and memory scaling, and interprets the new separation and timing analyses.

D1.justification: V2 adds dataset and code links, including a specific code revision, and identifies GPT-4o as the previously unspecified judge. It newly documents threshold-selection procedures, memory precision and footprint, batching restrictions, and guidance on samples needed for additional tasks. Existing hyperparameter values and hardware specifications are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds targeted discussion and citations for AQI, SafeSwitch, compliance-direction steering, SmoothLLM, and other safety research, and expands its treatment of FalseReject. It more explicitly criticizes task-agnostic mitigation, while retaining the original positioning around task-conditioned representation steering.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the methodology, dataset explanation, constellation analysis, and conclusion, and organizes the introduction around two explicit research questions. Memory Bank becomes Task Embeddings and Trajectory Health becomes Layer Alignment. Related-work subsections and appendix material are reorganized beyond the addition of scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 revises Figure 2 with clearer labels, a legend, and a workflow strip; adds latency and sample-level/separation figures plus a quantitative table; and moves v1's qualitative Table 3 into the appendix as Table 4. Typography, table formatting, and page layout are broadly revised. Most existing empirical graphics are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves auditability through code/data links and judge identification, adds quantitative evidence beyond v1's visual mechanism analysis, and states important applicability and evaluation limitations. These gains are qualified: Figure 14's metrics give mixed support for task-specific separation, and the revised algorithms are not explicitly reconciled with the unchanged efficacy results. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement in documentation and scientific qualification.
